name: Compact tetrahedron C(4,4;2,2;3,3)
description: Compact hyperbolic Coxeter tetrahedron with dihedral angles pi/2, pi/2, pi/3, pi/3, pi/4, pi/4. Every vertex stabilizer is B3 of order 48. The bundled PSL(2,7) x C2 kernel gives a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold tiled by 336 tetrahedra: the golden closed example for wall orientation plus the low-barycentric (IMM) subdivision in dimension 3.

geometry.source: Gram entries -cos(pi/m_ij) from the Coxeter matrix; normal coordinates are obtained numerically by the viewer's Lorentzian Gram factorization, so the placement is a drawing aid.

sourceRefs.citation: Bruno P. Zimmermann, Tetrahedral Coxeter groups, large group-actions on 3-manifolds and equivariant Heegaard splittings, Rendiconti dell'Istituto di Matematica dell'Universita di Trieste 52 (2020), 601-612; arXiv:2003.00730.
sourceRefs.locator: Discussion around Corollary 2.3: the C(4,4;2,2;3,3) kernel K_2, its PSL(2,7) quotient, and abelianization of free rank 13.
sourceRefs.notes: Supports the tetrahedron, the finite quotient, and b_1 = 13. The wall-orientation fibering computation is this repository's own.

sourceRefs.locator: Sections 1-2 for the Coxeter matrix labelling and the four projective involutions; sections 9-14 for the low-barycentric fibering argument.
sourceRefs.notes: In-repo writeup; its original computational artifacts are not in this repository.

notes: The bundled cover is the regular action of the image of s_i -> (r_i, 1) in PSL(2,7) x C2 (order 336); the in-repo certificate checks every spherical B3 restriction before calling the kernel torsion-free.

All 42 quotient walls are two-sided. tests/c44-golden-example.test.ts records a wall orientation whose low-barycentric subdivision passes both gates at every vertex (nonempty, connected, collapsible) with a nonzero wall class.
Gram signature and compactness are not certified by an in-repo checker for this example; the data status is verified-source, not certified.
warnings: Projected geometry is a drawing of chamber barycentres; it does not preserve hyperbolic distances or angles.
